items.guidance: This is a Go codebase despite the express label, so search the Go HTTP router setup (coderd) for existing unauthenticated routes such as /healthz or a build-info endpoint before adding anything. If one exists that returns 2xx without auth, report its path and leave code unchanged. Confirm the route is served on port 7080 and is not behind HTTPS or access-URL redirects.

Since this is a Go app, package.json is irrelevant; look for SQL migration files and Go code that applies them (for example a migrations package under the database code using golang-migrate) and check whether the server runs them automatically on startup. If startup applies migrations, report that file and propose no separate command. Report how the PostgreSQL connection URL is read, so it can be mapped to DATABASE_URL.

Check whether the dogfood Terraform files are Coder workspace templates or internal dogfooding infrastructure rather than files the server loads at runtime, and report what you find. Coder provisions workspaces through Terraform provisioners as a product feature, so also report whether the deployed server would need to execute Terraform against customer cloud infrastructure, since that may make it unhostable on Deployz.
